[[Sanfrecce Hiroshima|Sanfrecce]] vs. [[Cerezo Osaka|Cerezo]]) | average attendance = 18,428 | prevseason = [[2009 J.League Division 1|2009]] | nextseason = [[2011 J.League Division 1|2011]] }} The '''2010 J.League Division 1''' season was the 46th season of the top-flight club football in Japan and the 18th season since the establishment of [[J1 League]]. The season began on March 6 and ended on December 4.{{cite web|url=http://japantoday.com/category/sports/view/j-league-to-kick-off-season-march-6|title=J-League to kick off season March 6}}{{Dead link|date=April 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} A total of eighteen clubs participated in double round-robin format. At the end of the season, top three clubs received automatic qualification to the following years' [[AFC Champions League]]. Also, the bottom three clubs were relegated to [[J2 League]] by default. [[Nagoya Grampus]] won their first ever Japanese championship. This was also the first time since the advent of the J.League that the top scorer scored less than 20 goals; the honour of scoring 17 goals was shared between Nagoya's [[Joshua Kennedy]] and [[Júbilo Iwata]]'s [[Ryoichi Maeda]]. Marinos]] | {{flagicon|Argentina}} [[Pablo Bastianini]] | | | | | {{flagicon|South Korea}} [[Jeong Dong-ho]] | |} ==Format== Eighteen clubs will play in double round-robin (home and away) format, a total of 34 games each. A club receives 3 points for a win, 1 point for a tie, and 0 points for a loss. The clubs are ranked by points, and tie breakers are, in the following order: * Goal differential * Goals scored * Head-to-head results * Disciplinary points A draw would be conducted, if necessary. However, if two clubs are tied at the first place, both clubs will be declared as the champions. The bottom three clubs will be relegated to [[J2 League|J.League Division 2]]. The top three clubs will qualify to [[AFC Champions League]] in the following year. ;Changes from previous year * Regular season schedule had two months break after May 16 games, due to [[2010 FIFA World Cup]].
